claims.text: Overall Green Forest fire in France from 22 Jul 2026 00:00 UTC to 23 Jul 2026 00:00 UTC. Forest fire can have a low humanitarian impact based on the burned area and the affected population and their vulnerability. About 6,769 hectares burned and roughly 2,984 people in the affected area.

description: A fast-moving wildfire broke out in the Gironde department of southwestern France on 22 July 2026 and spread rapidly toward Bordeaux amid extreme heat and strong winds, prompting evacuation orders for suburbs on the city's western edge, including areas near its airport. GDACS escalated its alert from Green to Red as of episode 19 (27 July 2026); as of episode 22 (29 July 2026) the burned area stood at about 47,593 hectares with roughly 11,669 people in the fire-affected area and the alert remaining Red, with a thermal-anomaly detection recorded that same day, indicating the fire remains active. Widely reported figures — evacuations variously put at around 110,000 to 320,000+ people, French military mobilisation ordered by President Macron, and activation of the EU Civil Protection Mechanism — have not yet been confirmed by an allowlisted authoritative source.

impact.summary: GDACS's event report (eventid 1029628, episode 22) keeps this forest fire in France at an Overall Red alert, citing 47,593 hectares burned and 11,669 people in the fire-affected area, with the most recent thermal-anomaly detection on 29 July 2026 — up from 45,805 hectares/11,643 people affected as of episode 19 (27 July). No allowlisted authoritative source has yet published a confirmed death toll or evacuation count for this fire; widely reported figures of 110,000-320,000+ people evacuated, French military mobilisation, and EU Civil Protection Mechanism activation come from non-allowlisted media and have not been independently confirmed here.
